title: Flat-term K-flat models and the specified pulled reduction maps
statement:
Let $g:T'\to T$ be a morphism of schemes. Use the Noetherian adic datum $A,I,P_n=A/I^n$ ($n\geq1$), small pro-etale sites and coefficient sheaves of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. For $W=T,T'$ put $B_W=A_W=\varprojlim_n(P_n)_W$, $R_W=\underline A_W$ and $S_{n,W}=(P_n)_W$, with quotient ring maps $q_{b,a}$ for $b\geq a\geq1$. Use module pullbacks $g_R^*,g_n^*$ of [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback], exact scalar restriction $\operatorname{Res}$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], and unbounded module-sheaf derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

For every $K\in D(B_T)$, with no completeness or boundedness hypothesis, a complex representing $K$ admits a flat-term K-flat resolution $P$ [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. For every such $P$, $\operatorname{Res}P$ is K-flat with flat terms over $R_T$. More precisely, for every acyclic $R_T$-complex $E$, the canonical tensor identification
$$P\otimes_{R_T}E\cong P\otimes_{B_T}(B_T\otimes_{R_T}E)$$
has acyclic sides, $B_T\otimes_{R_T}E$ is acyclic, and each functor $P^i\otimes_{R_T}-$ is the composite of the exact functors $B_T\otimes_{R_T}-$ and $P^i\otimes_{B_T}-$. Tensor complexes use [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves].

Put $P_n=P\otimes_{B_T}S_{n,T}$, $U=g_R^*\operatorname{Res}P$, $Z_n=U\otimes_{R_{T'}}S_{n,T'}$ and $V_n=g_n^*P_n$. These are K-flat with flat terms over $S_{n,T},R_{T'},S_{n,T'},S_{n,T'}$, respectively; so are $Z_b\otimes_{S_{b,T'}}S_{a,T'}$ and $V_b\otimes_{S_{b,T'}}S_{a,T'}$. Their canonical representative identifications are isomorphisms in the respective derived categories with
$$K_n=K\otimes^L_{B_T}S_{n,T},\quad N=Lg_R^*\operatorname{Res}K,\quad N_n=N\otimes^L_{R_{T'}}S_{n,T'},\quad H_n=Lg_n^*K_n,$$
and with the corresponding successive derived scalar extensions. These assertions require no flatness of $S_{b,W}\to S_{a,W}$.

Write $[x]$ for a local inverse-image tensor generator from a local section $x$ of $P$, $e_n(x)=[x\otimes1]$ for its corresponding generator in $V_n$, and $\bar r_n$ for the image of a local $R_{T'}$-section $r$ in $S_{n,T'}$. Use actual sheaf tensor generators [def-weil-pbc-ringed-tensor-section-calculus]. The specified finite comparison $\tau_n:N_n\xrightarrow{\sim}H_n$ of [lem-weil-pbc-pulled-reduction-strict-tower-comparison] is represented by an isomorphism of sheaf tensor complexes
$$t_n:Z_n\xrightarrow{\sim}V_n,\qquad ([x]\otimes r)\otimes t\longmapsto e_n(x)\bar r_n t.$$
In this identification the finite constant-to-completed factor is the comparison $x\otimes t\mapsto x\otimes t$ over $R_T\to B_T\to S_{n,T}$; its multiplication map $B_T\otimes_{R_T}S_{n,T}\to S_{n,T}$ is invertible. The coefficient identifications are the canonical ones in [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence].

For $b\geq a\geq1$ define $h_{b,a}$ by the ordinary pullback/scalar comparison in the direction
$$V_b\otimes_{S_{b,T'}}S_{a,T'}\xrightarrow{\sim}g_a^*(P_b\otimes_{S_{b,T}}S_{a,T}),$$
followed by $g_a^*$ of the datum's balancing normalization. The first arrow is the inverse coequalizer comparison, equivalently the scalar-adjunction mate of [lem-sfb-kflat-scalar-comparison-normalization], under the canonical identifications $g^{-1}S_{j,T}=S_{j,T'}$. Both arrows are invertible. The composite is represented by
$$h_{b,a}:(e_b(x)t)\otimes s\longmapsto e_a(x)q_{b,a}(t)s,$$
with inverse $e_a(x)s\mapsto e_b(x)\otimes s$. Its localization is the specified derived comparison $\theta^H_{b,a}$: the pullback/scalar mate followed by $Lg_a^*$ of $K_b\otimes^L_{S_{b,T}}S_{a,T}\xrightarrow{\sim}K_a$. In particular this is an isomorphism in $D(S_{a,T'})$. Likewise
$$n_{b,a}:(u\otimes t)\otimes s\longmapsto u\otimes q_{b,a}(t)s$$
from $Z_b\otimes_{S_{b,T'}}S_{a,T'}$ to $Z_a$ represents the successive scalar normalization $\theta^N_{b,a}$ of [lem-sfb-successive-derived-quotient-normalization]. Before inverse image, the corresponding normalization is $(x\otimes t)\otimes s\mapsto x\otimes q_{b,a}(t)s$, with inverse $x\otimes s\mapsto(x\otimes1)\otimes s$. All displayed formulas define balanced, restriction-compatible morphisms of the actual sheaf tensor complexes, with the stated inverses, rather than only maps on degreewise cohomology.

proof.text: Choose a complex representing $K$. Apply [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] on the small ringed site $(T_{\mathrm{proet}},B_T)$ to obtain a quasi-isomorphism $P\to K$ with $P$ K-flat and every $P^i$ flat. This existence theorem is for arbitrary cochain complexes, so neither boundedness nor derived completeness is required.

source.place: Tags 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution), 0G7E (lemma-pullback-K-flat), 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change); tensor balancing as specified below

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence], $B_T$ is flat over $R_T$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-flat-scalar-restriction-kflat] gives K-flatness and flat terms for $\operatorname{Res}P$. For the more explicit assertion, if $E$ is acyclic over $R_T$, exactness of $B_T\otimes_{R_T}-$ and [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] imply that $B_T\otimes_{R_T}E$ is acyclic over $B_T$. The tensor cancellation of [lem-pur-change-of-rings-tensor-cancellation-independent], applied to $P^i,E^j$, gives the stated tensor identification. It extends to total complexes: distribute tensor over the direct sums using [lem-weil-pbc-independent-sheaf-tensor-colimits]; the degreewise maps preserve both tensor differentials and their signs [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. K-flatness of $P$ makes its right side acyclic. For a single term $P^i$ the same identification factors $P^i\otimes_{R_T}-$ as the two exact functors displayed in the statement, by the definition of flatness [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules].

source.place: Tags 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution), 0G7E (lemma-pullback-K-flat), 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change); tensor balancing as specified below

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat] first to the identity geometric inverse image with coefficient map $B_T\to S_{n,T}$, giving $P_n$, and to $g$ with constant coefficients $R_T,R_{T'}$, giving $U$. Apply it next to $R_{T'}\to S_{n,T'}$ on the identity topos, giving $Z_n$, and to $g$ with coefficients $S_{n,T},S_{n,T'}$, giving $V_n$. Finally apply it to each identity-topos map $S_{b,T'}\to S_{a,T'}$ with inputs $Z_b,V_b$. Apply it also to the identity-topos maps $R_T\to S_{n,T}$ with input $\operatorname{Res}P$ and $S_{b,T}\to S_{a,T}$ with input $P_b$; then apply it to $g$ with coefficients $S_{n,T},S_{n,T'}$ (resp. $S_{a,T},S_{a,T'}$) to the resulting complexes $\operatorname{Res}P\otimes_{R_T}S_{n,T}$ and $P_b\otimes_{S_{b,T}}S_{a,T}$. Every input is K-flat with flat terms by the preceding applications. This proves all claimed K-flat and termwise-flat properties; the cited theorem explicitly imposes no flatness on the coefficient map.

proof.text: The representative comparisons of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] identify $P_n,Z_n$ with $K_n,N_n$, and identify the tensors of $Z_b,V_b$ with the corresponding successive derived scalar extensions. The representative comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback] identifies $U$ with $N$, $V_n$ with $H_n$, $g_n^*(\operatorname{Res}P\otimes_{R_T}S_{n,T})$ with $Lg_n^*(\operatorname{Res}K\otimes^L_{R_T}S_{n,T})$ and $g_a^*(P_b\otimes_{S_{b,T}}S_{a,T})$ with $Lg_a^*(K_b\otimes^L_{S_{b,T}}S_{a,T})$; by its naturality in maps of such resolutions, $g^*$ of a chain map between these flat-term K-flat models represents $Lg^*$ of its localization. All its hypotheses hold by steps 1–3. Exact scalar restriction [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars] carries $P\to K$ to a quasi-isomorphism, so $\operatorname{Res}P$ represents $\operatorname{Res}K$. These are isomorphisms in the module-sheaf derived categories, before taking any cohomology.

proof.text: Write $R=R_T$, $B=B_T$, $S=S_{n,T}$. The canonical quotient identification $B/I^nB=S$ in [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence] makes multiplication $B\otimes_R S\to S$ invertible. Indeed $S=R/I^nR$, so balancing identifies $B\otimes_R S$ with $B/I^nB$; the inverse sends $s$ to $1\otimes s$. For every $B$-module $M$, cancellation [lem-pur-change-of-rings-tensor-cancellation-independent] now identifies $\operatorname{Res}M\otimes_R S$ with $M\otimes_B S$. The forward map is $x\otimes t\mapsto x\otimes t$. For its inverse, the relation $(bx)\otimes t=x\otimes\bar b t$ holds already over $R$: multiply $b\otimes t=1\otimes\bar b t$ in $B\otimes_R S$ against $x$. Hence this is a balanced inverse, not a choice of lifts of sections. These maps are maps of actual sheaf tensors by [def-weil-pbc-ringed-tensor-section-calculus], and apply in every degree of $P$.

source.place: Tag 093M (lemma-completion-flat), applied also to powers of I; Tag 05V4 tensor cancellation; elementary quotient balancing

proof.text: Use the inverse coequalizer comparison of [lem-sfb-kflat-scalar-comparison-normalization] for $R_T\to S_{n,T}$ and $g$, then apply $g_n^*$ to the isomorphism in step 5. After the canonical constant coefficient identifications this is $t_n:Z_n\to V_n$, with formula $([x]\otimes r)\otimes t\mapsto e_n(x)\bar r_n t$. Its inverse sends $e_n(x)t$ to $([x]\otimes1)\otimes t$. Balancing gives $([x]\otimes r)\otimes t=([x]\otimes1)\otimes\bar r_n t$, so both composites are identities. Additivity, all coefficient relations, and restrictions are preserved by the two constituent sheaf tensor maps [def-weil-pbc-ringed-tensor-section-calculus]. Their formulas commute with $d_P$, hence define an isomorphism of complexes. For the second factor apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-coefficient-reduction-adjunct] to $R_T\to B_T\to S_{n,T}$: $B_T$ is $R_T$-flat (step 2) and the multiplication $B_T\otimes_{R_T}S_{n,T}\to S_{n,T}$ is invertible (step 5). Its canonical balanced comparison $\kappa_{K,S_{n,T}}:\operatorname{Res}K\otimes^L_{R_T}S_{n,T}\to K_n$, the canonical finite constant-to-completed comparison, is represented on $P$ by $x\otimes t\mapsto x\otimes t$, i.e. by the isomorphism of step 5. By step 4 $g_n^*$ of that isomorphism represents $Lg_n^*\kappa$, and the cited scalar-mate identification represents the pullback/scalar comparison by the inverse coequalizer comparison. Hence the localization of $t_n$ is precisely the specified finite comparison $\tau_n$: its two factors are the pullback/scalar comparison and the finite constant-to-completed comparison, in that order.

source.place: Tags 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution), 0G7E (lemma-pullback-K-flat), 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change); tensor balancing as specified below

proof.text: For $S_{b,T}\to S_{a,T}$, [lem-sfb-kflat-scalar-comparison-normalization] identifies the inverse coequalizer comparison on $P_b$ with the derived scalar-adjunction mate. It sends $(e_b(x)t)\otimes s$ to the inverse-image tensor represented by $(x\otimes t)\otimes s$. Apply $g_a^*$ of the datum's balancing normalization [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], which sends this to $e_a(x)q_{b,a}(t)s$. This is $h_{b,a}$. Its inverse sends $e_a(x)s$ to $e_b(x)\otimes s$: in the other composite the balancing equality $(e_b(x)t)\otimes s=e_b(x)\otimes q_{b,a}(t)s$ recovers the original tensor. These relations also prove additivity and balancing for the inverse. By [def-weil-pbc-ringed-tensor-section-calculus] the maps commute with restrictions and, by their formulas, with differentials. Step 4 identifies their localizations with the pullback/scalar mate followed by $Lg_a^*$ of the datum normalization. Thus the specified $\theta^H_{b,a}$, rather than an unspecified isomorphism with the same endpoints, is invertible.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-successive-derived-quotient-normalization] to $R_{T'}\to S_{b,T'}\to S_{a,T'}$ with K-flat representative $U$. It states that $n_{b,a}$ is exactly $(u\otimes t)\otimes s\mapsto u\otimes q_{b,a}(t)s$, representing $\theta^N_{b,a}$, with inverse $u\otimes s\mapsto(u\otimes1)\otimes s$. Apply the same theorem to $B_T\to S_{b,T}\to S_{a,T}$ with representative $P$ for the before-inverse-image normalization and its inverse. Its statement gives these formulas and inverses as sheaf-complex maps. Together with steps 5–7 this proves the balanced, restriction-compatible complex assertions for every displayed map. No argument used flatness of a quotient transition.

B⊗_R S_n ≅ S_n follows from B/I^nB=S_n, and I verified the balancing of the inverse. I recomputed χ^{-1}, giving t_n=e_n(x)\bar r t and h_{b,a}=e_a(x)q(t)s with their inverses, and n_{b,a} comes from successive-normalization. Edge cases checked: K=0, I=0, I=A, b=a, g=id, and the non-flat case ℤ/ℓ²→ℤ/ℓ. I found no duplicate. The generic off-unit tool uses are accepted. Its hypotheses (B flat over R, from step 2, and B⊗_R S→S invertible, from step 5) give κ represented by x⊗s↦x⊗s. The base parent step 3 had cited this node and the delivery had dropped it.
